subject: SLA / Renewal risk: Production latency & errors from dedicated pool saturation
messages:
From: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@finvera.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — reserved throughput unmet (urgent)

Jonas —

We started seeing sustained token latency spikes and 5xx errors across our production endpoints starting ~08:30 PST this morning. Our metrics show request queueing growth, median response time jumped from ~150ms to ~1.9s and error rate climbed to 4.6% (was <0.5%). We are on your Reserved plan (25k tokens/s) and this is impacting our customer-facing flows; we have a renewal review next week.

Can you confirm what happened and what the timeline is for remediation? We need immediate mitigation (fallback, throttle) and a clear post-incident plan. If this continues, we will have to escalate internally on our side.

Attached: snippet of failed request ids and timestamps.

—Rajesh
VP Engineering, FinVera
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@finvera.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — reserved throughput unmet (urgent)

Rajesh — thanks for flagging, and sorry for the disruption. I’m escalating immediately to our on-call ops and product leads (cc'd). We’re treating this as a P1. Initial steps I’ve kicked off:

- Naomi is pulling detailed traces and queue metrics (logs attached when ready).
- We’ve initiated a temporary routing rule to divert non-critical traffic to a lower-cost fallback model to reduce pressure on your dedicated pool.
- I’ll propose an exec-level mitigation (burst capacity) if we can’t stabilize in the next 2 hours.

Can you confirm any recent spike in QPS from your side (jobs, batch replays) or a release that might have increased sequence lengths? Any context helps the triage.

I’ll keep you updated every 30 minutes until we’re stable.

—Jonas
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@finvera.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — reserved throughput unmet (urgent)

On Tue, Oct 9, 2028 at 09:15 AM Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@finvera.com> wrote:
> Jonas —
> We started seeing sustained token latency spikes and 5xx errors across our production endpoints starting ~08:30 PST this morning...

Quick triage summary (initial 30m):
- Observed: sustained GPU utilization at 98% across the assigned dedicated pool + request queue length growth. Autoscaling did not add additional nodes because the pool configuration has a hard cap at reserved capacity (no burst configured).
- Error type: transient OOM-like rejections and RPC timeouts linked to long-context requests producing large KV cache churn.
- Impact: FinVera route consuming ~3x expected tail-sequence tokens/min for the last 90 minutes.

Immediate mitigation applied (09:35):
1) Activated routing to fallback model (reduced quality) for non-critical routes — rolled back heavy batch jobs for FinVera.
2) Throttled concurrency per-connection to blunt queue growth.
3) Collected logs and exported queue traces (attached: log_export_20281009.csv).

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Short term (now–4h): temporary 2x burst capacity (requires exec approval) or manual reallocation from other non-critical pools. ETA to stabilize if approved: ~45–90 minutes after capacity provision.
- Mid term (24–72h): rollout rollback of the new model variant for FinVera or apply quantization config to reduce memory pressure.

I’ve uploaded a quick SLA impact snapshot (SLA_report_Q3_2028.pdf) to the shared drive and included the mitigation runbook.

—Naomi
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@finvera.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — reserved throughput unmet (urgent)

On Tue, Oct 9, 2028 at 09:48 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick triage summary...

Adding product context: we pushed a model variant last week that increases context window by default for certain prompts; it appears FinVera’s traffic pattern (longer conversation histories) is causing a much higher KV cache miss rate and memory churn on the Dedicated runtime. That, combined with their reserved pool config (no burst elastic capacity), is exposing throughput limits.

Temporary technical options (pick 1–2 now):
- Roll back FinVera to previous model variant (risk: quality delta) — low-risk, fast (30–60m).
- Enable emergency quantization mode for the route — moderate risk, medium time to apply (90m).
- Approve immediate burst capacity purchase (recommended if rollback unacceptable).

Operational ask: I need executive sign-off to provision a 30% short-term capacity burst (estimate $35k/month pro-rated) while we execute rollback/quantization. If approved, we’ll provision and then deprovision within 5 business days unless a longer commit is negotiated.

—Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@finvera.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Exec approval request — emergency burst & customer credit to avoid renewal fallout

Marissa / Aditya —

FinVera (FV-2027-EXP-04) is experiencing a P1 tied to dedicated-pool saturation and reserved throughput shortfall. Impact: production latency & errors for customer-critical flows, renewal meeting next Tuesday. Triage indicates the root cause is higher-than-normal long-context token churn after our recent model variant rollout.

We propose the following emergency package to stabilize and retain the account:
1) Immediate 30% burst capacity (pro-rated ~$35k/mo) for 48–72h to eliminate queueing while we rollback/quantize. Requires exec sign-off to provision.
2) Offer FinVera a one-time customer credit equal to 20% of October invoice as a goodwill gesture and to reduce renewal friction (estimate $Xk).
3) Commit to a detailed post-mortem and a cadence of remediation: model rollback within 4h if approved, production verification, and a follow-up technical review with FinVera by EOD tomorrow.

Why approve: Without fast mitigation we risk an at-risk renewal and an Executive escalation from FinVera. With the package we buy time to remediate, keep production stable, and preserve the relationship.

Request: approve the burst now and the proposed credit. Please reply with approval/decline in the next 30 minutes so we can act.

—Jonas
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@finvera.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec approval request — emergency burst & customer credit to avoid renewal fallout

- Authorize the 30% burst for 72 hours immediately. Procurement/finance: please triage the short-term commitment and confirm billing flow.
- Approve 20% one-time credit to FinVera as a retention gesture. Finance, please draft the credit note and run by legal.

Jonas/Naomi/Karthik: keep the customer updated with concrete timings. I want a post-mortem in 48 hours and the remediation plan in writing. Loop me if FinVera escalates to their execs.

—Marissa Cole
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
